bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar CM says Constitution strengthens democratic traditions, inspires national unity
bihar_raw_news.content: Governance 1 min Read Bihar CM says Constitution strengthens democratic traditions, inspires national unity "Our Constitution, based on the fundamental ideals of justice, liberty, equality and fraternity, is not merely the foundation of the country's system of governance, but also the guardian of every citizen's rights, duties and dignity," Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary said. PTI Published On Nov 26, 2026 at 11:32 PM IST Set ETGovernment as your preferred source on Google Share Icon Copy Link Share on Whatsapp Share on Linkedin Share on X Share on Telegram Share on Facebook Bookmark Comment Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary on Thursday urged people to uphold the core values of the Constitution , including justice, liberty, equality and fraternity, saying it is not merely the foundation of the country's governance system but also the guardian of every citizen's rights, duties and dignity. On the occasion of Constitution Day , he led a padayatra covering around 2 km in Bettiah town of West Champaran district - from Sagar Pokhra to Raj Deorhi. NDA workers and supporters from surrounding assembly constituencies also took part in the procession. Choudhary addressed party workers at Raj Deorhi, highlighting the importance of constitutional values, democratic institutions and national unity . Earlier in the day, in a post on X on the occasion of Constitution Day, he said the Constitution strengthens India's democratic traditions and inspires the nation to preserve its unity and integrity. "Our Constitution, based on the fundamental ideals of justice, liberty, equality and fraternity, is not merely the foundation of the country's system of governance, but also the guardian of every citizen's rights, duties and dignity," the CM said. "It inspires us to uphold the country's unity and integrity while strengthening our democratic traditions. On the occasion of Constitution Day, let us all resolve to embrace the ideals and values enshrined in the Constitution in our lives, remain committed to democratic values, and further strengthen the spirit of fraternity and national unity," he added. India observes Constitution Day, also known as Samvidhan Diwas , every year on November 26 to commemorate the adoption of the Constitution by the Constituent Assembly on November 26, 1949. The Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs (CCEA) , chaired by Prime Minister Narendra Modi, approved the development of a second container terminal at Kamarajar Port Limited (KPL), Tamil Nadu , on 25 November 2026. Key Points: Project Overview: The project involves developing a 900-metre-long second container terminal at Kamarajar Port. Annual container-handling capacity: 2 million Twenty-foot Equivalent Units (TEUs) . It will be developed in two phases: Phase I: Capacity of 1.1 million TEUs. Phase II: Capacity of 0.9 million TEUs. Press Information Bureau Implementation Model – DBFOT: The project will follow the Design, Build, Finance, Operate and Transfer (DBFOT) model. The private concessionaire will design, construct, finance and operate the terminal. The concession period will be 40 years , including a construction period of 48 months. Capacity to Handle Large Container Vessels: The new terminal is designed to accommodate large mainline container ships. It will be capable of handling vessels of up to 24,346 TEUs and 400 metres in length. The 18-metre design draft will enable larger vessels to access the terminal. Existing Performance of Kamarajar Port: Handled 49.08 million tonnes of cargo and 1,008 vessels during FY 2025–26. Container traffic exceeded 7 lakh TEUs during the same period. Existing container terminal capacity: 0.8 million TEUs annually. Actual container handling: approximately 0.7 million TEUs, representing around 88% capacity utilisation . Container traffic at Kamarajar Port grew at approximately 9.9% CAGR over the preceding five years, compared with around 7% growth nationally. Alignment with National Maritime Initiatives: Maritime India Vision 2030: Aims to enhance port infrastructure, maritime trade and logistics efficiency. Maritime Amrit Kaal Vision 2047: Provides a long-term framework for developing India's maritime sector. Atmanirbhar Bharat: The project will strengthen domestic port capacity and reduce dependence on foreign transshipment infrastructure. About Kamarajar Port Limited: Formerly known as Ennore Port Limited . Located on the eastern coast of Tamil Nadu, near the Chennai industrial region. It is wholly owned by Chennai Port Authority under the Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways. It handles coal, petroleum products, LNG, LPG, containers, automobiles and general cargo. During FY 2025–26, it recorded revenue of approximately ₹1,280 crore and profit before tax of ₹924 crore. bihar_raw_news.title: Delhi- Bihar Bus Network to Add 18 Year-Round Routes
bihar_raw_news.content: Home Breaking News Delhi-Bihar Bus Network to Add 18 Year-Round Routes Breaking News Delhi-Bihar Bus Network to Add 18 Year-Round Routes By Ananya Sharma November 27, 2026 0 Copy URL Facebook Linkedin X WhatsApp Delhi and Bihar are set to introduce year-round interstate bus services on 18 routes, with around 200 AC and non-AC buses connecting the national capital with destinations across Bihar, Delhi Transport Minister Pankaj Singh said on Thursday. The services are expected to benefit nearly 20 lakh people from Bihar and Purvanchal who live and work in Delhi, as well as other passengers travelling between the two states. The proposed network is being introduced under a reciprocal transport agreement between Delhi and Bihar. Officials said the services are likely to be inaugurated on Friday, although operating timings have not yet been finalised. Fares are expected to be around Rs 2,000 to Rs 3,000 for sleeper and non-sleeper categories. The routes will connect Delhi with destinations including Araria, Bhagalpur, Buxar, Darbhanga, East Champaran, Gaya, Kishanganj, Madhubani, Muzaffarpur, Nawada, Patna and Purnia. The report also refers to destinations in the Bhagalpur region. Singh said the agreement would provide more convenient and accessible travel, particularly during peak seasons when passengers face heavy rush and limited train-ticket availability. The services are also intended to ease overcrowding on existing bus connections during festivals and other periods of high demand. To expand interstate transport capacity, the Bihar State Road Transport Corporation has procured 75 non-AC and 74 AC buses for interstate operations, officials said. A further 150 buses are expected to be deployed through the public-private partnership model. Officials described the planned services as an environment-friendly public-transport initiative that would strengthen connectivity between Delhi and Bihar. The final schedule, route-wise frequency and operational arrangements had not been announced in the report. national_raw_news.title: US proposes fresh tariffs on imports from 14 economies, including India
national_raw_news.content: United States has proposed fresh tariffs ranging from 15 to 35 per cent on imports from 14 economies, including China, the European Union and India. The other economies covered include Taiwan, Singapore, Switzerland, Indonesia, Malaysia, Cambodia, Thailand, South Korea, Bangladesh and Japan. US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer today said the proposed measures are aimed at addressing policies that Washington believes disadvantage American manufacturers and weaken the country’s industrial base. China could face tariffs of up to 40 per cent, while Vietnam may face duties of up to 35 per cent. The proposals include exemptions for certain products, such as semiconductors and other high-tech goods from Taiwan and South Korea. The duties will not take effect immediately. For India, the USTR has proposed tariffs of up to 25 per cent on goods, after accounting for existing Section 301 duties, with exemptions for certain products. It has also proposed considering a 17 per cent rate if India reaches a reciprocal trade agreement with the US that addresses the findings of the investigation. The US administration has invited public comments until 5th January next year, with hearings scheduled to begin on 25th January. The proposed tariffs could come into force as early as February next year. Meanwhile, the European Union and China have rejected Washington’s allegations of excessive industrial production. The European Commission said it would examine Washington’s justification for the move. It noted that tariffs on European goods are capped at 15 per cent under the existing trade agreement with the United States.

national_raw_news.title: India wins Best National Pavilion – Visitors’ Lion award at Venice Art Biennale
national_raw_news.content: India has won the Best National Pavilion – Visitors’ Lion at the Venice Art Biennale, the Olympics of the art world. The honour was decided through votes by visitors from across the globe and is a recognition of India’s growing cultural influence. Expressing happiness, Prime Minister Narendra Modi called it a proud moment for India’s art and cultural world. In a social media post, Prime Minister Modi said India’s artists are bringing fresh perspectives to the world of art, drawing inspiration from India’s rich and diverse cultural heritage. He wished that this feat would inspire many more young Indians to pursue art and explore new creative horizons. Culture and Tourism Minister Gajendra Singh Shekhawat has said, this global recognition is a testament to the talent of new-age Indian artists and the vibrancy of the nation’s contemporary art scene. He said, this award celebrates how India’s timeless artistic traditions can find powerful contemporary expression and resonate with audiences across the world. Mr Shekhawat said that the honour will inspire generations of Indian artists to engage with the world with greater confidence and creativity. Housed at the historic Arsenale, the India Pavilion was commissioned by the National Gallery of Modern Art, Ministry of Culture, with the Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts serving as the executing agency.

national_raw_news.title: PM Modi calls for strengthening constitutional values and placing India First in national endeavours
national_raw_news.content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi has said that over the past decade, Government has laid special emphasis on Kartavya, or the duties of a citizen. He said, Indian civilisation has always emphasised the responsibilities that accompany every role in society. In an op-ed in daily newspapers in English and Hindi today on Constitution Day, Mr Modi said, the spirit of Kartavya has found expression in several mass movements, from Swachh Bharat to water conservation and environmental protection. Prime Minister Narendra Modi today called upon citizens to uphold the spirit of the Constitution and work collectively towards building a developed India by 2047. In an op-ed in daily newspapers in English and Hindi Mr Modi recalled the adoption of the Constitution in 1949. He noted that the Constitution must find resonance beyond Parliament and the courts and become an integral part of the collective consciousness of citizens, particularly the youth. He said the decision to observe 26 November as Constitution Day was aimed at deepening people’s connection with the Constitution. Paying tribute to Dr. Rajendra Prasad, Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar and all members of the Constituent Assembly, Mr Modi said that their greatness lay in drawing extensively from the rich traditions and civilisational wisdom of Bharat while framing a modern Constitution. He emphasised that it is important that the Constitution have a resonance far beyond the precincts of Parliament and the courts. Sharing his personal journey, the Prime Minister said the Constitution had made it possible for a person born into a family of modest means, with no privileges or advantages of birth, to shoulder the responsibility of serving the world’s largest democracy. Mr. Modi described various government initiatives, including PM Awas Yojana, Ujjwala Yojana, Ayushman Bharat, MUDRA and PM-SVANidhi, as measures aimed at improving the lives of disadvantaged sections and expanding opportunities. Referring to a recent World Bank report, the Prime Minister said nearly 50 crore Indians had moved out of poverty. He noted that digital technology and platforms like UPI transcend all divides and place opportunities once available to a privileged few within the reach of every citizen, advancing the constitutional ideal of inclusivity. Mr. Modi said the abrogation of Articles 370 and 35A in 2019 enabled the full implementation of the Constitution in Jammu and Kashmir, extending constitutional rights to all sections of society. Highlighting the successful elimination of Naxalism, the Prime Minister said that the government has ensured that the poorest of the poor can finally exercise their constitutional rights without fear. Mr Modi further added that the journey of our Constitution would be incomplete without recognising the remarkable women who helped shape it. Mr Modi accused the Opposition of seeking to curtail reservation for Other Backward Classes (OBC) to introduce quotas for Muslims. He said, it is most appalling that the biggest party in the Opposition wants to reduce OBC reservation and bring Muslim reservations, something the makers of the Constitution, notably Dr Babasaheb Ambedkar, were totally against. The Prime Minister said, the country’s constitutional democracy has a clearly defined role for the Opposition. He said, sadly, the leading Opposition party seems to have become more of an obstructionist than a opposition. Mr Modi said, they should know that disrupting democratic processes is no substitute for discharging constitutional responsibilities.

national_raw_news.content: The Constitution Day (Samvidhan Diwas) is being observed today to commemorate the adoption of the Constitution of India by the Constituent Assembly on 26th November, 1949. The day has been observed as Constitution Day since 2015. Constitution Day provides an occasion to reflect upon the principles and values enshrined in the Constitution of India and to renew the collective commitment to its ideals. The observance seeks to strengthen constitutional awareness, promote responsible citizenship and encourage active participation in upholding the democratic values of the nation. On the occasion, the Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs is facilitating an online reading of the Preamble to the Constitution through the MyGov portal in 23 languages, comprising 22 Scheduled Languages and English. This initiative will provide an opportunity to citizens across the country to read the Preamble and reaffirm their commitment to the ideals and values enshrined in the Constitution. Various activities are being organised across the country by Ministries and Departments of the Government, State and Union Territories Governments, autonomous bodies and institutions to mark the occasion. These activities include collective reading of the Preamble, seminars, webinars, quizzes, essay and debate competitions, poster-making, cultural programmes, awareness campaigns, walks, runs and other community engagement activities. The Ministry noted that various awareness and outreach activities are also being undertaken through digital platforms and community-based initiatives to promote understanding of the Constitution and its significance in the country’s democratic framework.

national_raw_news.title: WAVES Film Bazaar at IFFI in Goa attracts 2,288 delegates from 54 countries
national_raw_news.content: In the ongoing International Film Festival of India (IFFI), in Goa, key outcomes were announced yesterday from the recently concluded WAVES Film Bazaar, alongside vibrant cultural celebrations and special sessions honouring legendary voices of Indian cinema. In today’s events, exciting masterclasses and special film screenings are lined up promising another engaging chapter in the festival. Two Letters of Intent for India-Chile co-productions have emerged as a major outcome of the 20th edition of the WAVES Film Bazaar, while 14 Memoranda of Understanding and agreements are nearing finalisation. Addressing a press conference in Goa yesterday, Additional Secretary in the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting, Prabhat, said that WAVES Film Bazaar brought together 2 thousand 288 delegates from 54 countries, including 471 buyers. He added that the Bazaar also facilitated around 220 business-to-business meetings, this year. The festival also experienced a colourful IFFI Parade in Panaji, celebrating Goa’s cultural heritage through vibrant floats and folk performances. While the Aakash Kandil Competition added a creative spark to the celebrations, showcasing colourful lanterns inspired by IFFI’s Peacock mascot. The 6th day also witnessed acclaimed playback singer K. S. Chithra paying tributes to legendary singers Lata Mangeshkar, Asha Bhosle and S. Janaki during a special session. Meanwhile, today, the seventh day promises an exciting line-up of events, including masterclasses by casting director Mukesh Chhabra on auditioning and actor selection, and Natalie Wade of the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences on the Academy Awards. Special screenings will include Rishab Shetty’s Kantara: A Legend Chapter 1, and the Marathi film Tu Aahes Na as a gala presentation

national_raw_news.title: Constitution Day to Be Observed Across India on November 26
national_raw_news.content: Constitution Day, or Samvidhan Diwas, will be observed across the country on November 26 to mark the adoption of the Constitution of India by the Constituent Assembly on November 26, 1949. The day has been observed as Constitution Day since 2015 to promote awareness about the Constitution and reaffirm the country’s commitment to its democratic values and principles. As part of this year’s celebrations, the Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs is facilitating an online reading of the Preamble to the Constitution through the MyGov portal in 23 languages, including 22 Scheduled Languages and English. Citizens can participate by reading the Preamble, downloading a participation certificate and sharing it on social media. The celebrations also include a Constitution Quiz being conducted through the MyGov and MyBharat portals from November 18 to 26. In addition, Viksit Bharat Yuva Samvad is being organised across 786 districts in all 36 States and Union Territories from November 24 to 26 to encourage greater participation among young people. Several activities are being organised by Central Ministries and Departments, State and Union Territory governments, educational institutions and other organisations. These include collective readings of the Preamble, seminars, webinars, quizzes, essay and debate competitions, poster-making, cultural programmes, awareness campaigns, walks and community engagement initiatives. Schools, colleges and universities have also been encouraged to organise special morning assemblies, discussions and competitions to familiarise students with the making of the Constitution and its key features. With a special focus on grassroots participation, the celebrations aim to strengthen constitutional awareness among citizens, particularly young people and students, through digital platforms and community-based outreach programmes. Constitution Day serves as an occasion to reflect on the ideals of justice, liberty, equality and fraternity enshrined in the Constitution and renew the collective commitment to upholding the country’s democratic framework.

national_raw_news.title: PM chairs 55th PRAGATI meeting
national_raw_news.content: Prime Minister's Office PM chairs 55th PRAGATI meeting PM reviews five infrastructure projects in the road, power, coal and railway sectors worth over ₹78,000 crore PM stresses on timely execution accompanied by high standards of construction quality PM also reviews the ITI ecosystem including the implementation of PM-SETU PM calls for stronger PSU–ITI linkages and skilling aligned with industrial clusters and sectoral needs PM advocates the 3C approach of Classroom–Company–Career to connect training with employment PM notes that stronger links between ITIs and local employers could expand employment opportunities closer to home Posted On: 25 NOV 2026 9:07PM by PIB Delhi Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi chaired the 55th meeting of PRAGATI, the ICT-enabled, multi-modal platform aimed at fostering Pro-Active Governance and Timely Implementation, at Seva Teerth earlier today. The platform brings together the Central and State Governments to address implementation bottlenecks and improve the delivery of projects and welfare schemes. During the meeting, the Prime Minister reviewed five critical infrastructure projects in the road, power, coal and railway sectors, with a total cost of over ₹78,000 crore. He also reviewed the Industrial Training Institute (ITI) ecosystem, including the implementation of the Pradhan Mantri Skilling and Employability Transformation through Upgraded ITIs (PM-SETU). Prime Minister emphasised that delays in infrastructure projects have consequences beyond cost escalation, as they postpone the benefits intended for citizens, businesses and the economy. He called upon the concerned Ministries and State Governments to resolve pending issues with clear responsibility and realistic timelines. He stressed that timely execution must be accompanied by high standards of construction quality. Reviewing the road project, the Prime Minister called for expeditious implementation and reiterated the need to focus on outcomes over outlays. While reviewing the coal project, the Prime Minister emphasised that rehabilitation and resettlement should be undertaken in a timely and dignified manner alongside timely project implementation. While reviewing the power project, the Prime Minister suggested exploring innovative models for decentralised solar and wind power projects. He emphasised that such projects should be developed closer to centres of consumption wherever feasible, taking into account local resource availability and demand. These efforts should aim to improve the availability of reliable and affordable power and ease pressure on transmission infrastructure. Reviewing the ITI ecosystem and the implementation of PM-SETU, Prime Minister called upon Chief Ministers and Chief Secretaries to provide leadership in strengthening ITIs and deepening industry participation under PM-SETU. He emphasised that this was an opportune time for industry to partner with ITIs, contribute to their upgradation and help align training with current and future manpower requirements. He called for close collaboration between States, ITIs and industry to translate these partnerships into better training and employment opportunities for young people. Prime Minister called upon Public Sector Undertakings (PSUs) to assess their future manpower requirements and strengthen linkages with ITIs for training and recruitment in relevant trades. national_raw_news.content: Rajnath Singh calls for stronger strategic preparedness, actionable research to address emerging national security challenges at NDC Toggle navigation हिंदी खबर Rajnath Singh calls for stronger strategic preparedness, actionable research to address emerging national security challenges at NDC ANI | Updated: Nov 26, 2026 18:38 IST ANI News Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [India], November 26 (ANI): Defence Minister Rajnath Singh has called for anticipating emerging risks, examining alternative scenarios and preparing institutions for the security environment of the future, while ensuring an effective response to immediate threats arising from evolving geopolitical dynamics and the changing nature of warfare. Addressing the Convocation & Valedictory Ceremony of the 66th National Defence College (NDC) Course in New Delhi on Thursday, he asserted that the evolving global balance of power, emergence of new centres of strategic influence and recalibration of traditional alliances, coupled with the changing nature of conflict, have made the security environment increasingly complex. The Defence Minister said that conventional military threats are increasingly co-existing with cyber-attacks, disinformation, economic coercion, disruptions to supply chains and other forms of hybrid warfare, blurring the boundaries between internal and external security, and peace & conflict. He emphasised that India's geographical location, extensive land borders, maritime interests and growing international responsibilities place it in a complex strategic environment, necessitating a forward-looking approach to national security. Stressing the need to connect strategic learning with national security policymaking, Rajnath Singh said NDC provides a valuable platform to harness the collective professional experience and intellectual capabilities of senior officers from the Defence Forces, Civil Services and friendly countries. He pitched for greater utilisation of this intellectual capital to contribute directly to India's national security policymaking. The Defence Minister suggested that NDC, in consultation with the Ministry of Defence, institutionalise a mechanism to identify a few significant contemporary national security challenges for intensive examination during every course. These could relate to India's strategic neighbourhood, border management, maritime security, critical technologies, economic security, protection of critical infrastructure and evolving internal and external threats, he said. Rajnath Singh also urged NDC to develop a mechanism through which serving senior military officers, civil servants and other relevant authorities are invited to formally pose specific contemporary challenges confronting the nation for examination by the course participants. “The challenges could be drawn from actual operational, strategic, administrative and policy concerns being faced by different Ministries & organisations. This would bring real-world issues into the academic framework of NDC and provide an opportunity to examine them from multiple perspectives,” he said. Underlining the need to translate academic research into actionable policy inputs, the Defence Minister emphasised that research undertaken by course participants should not remain confined to academic papers or classroom discussions. He stressed that selected studies should culminate in comprehensive reports containing specific, practical and actionable recommendations. These, he said, should be formally submitted to the Ministry of Defence and other concerned Ministries, wherever relevant, and presented before appropriate levels of Government for consideration. national_raw_news.content: IndiaAI Mission Marks New Milestone With Launch Of Indigenous Chariot-1 Language And Speech Models Tech IndiaAI Mission Marks New Milestone With Launch Of Indigenous Chariot-1 Language And Speech Models Swarajya Staff Nov 26, 2026 | Updated 04:04 PM GMT+5:30 Save & read from anywhere! Bookmark stories for easy access on any device or the Swarajya app . Sign In Prefer Prefer Pic Via PIB India strengthened its sovereign artificial intelligence capabilities today (26 November) with the launch of Chariot-1 foundation models under the IndiaAI Mission. Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology Secretary S Krishnan launched the models alongside a research showcase at an event in New Delhi, marking a significant milestone in India's indigenous AI development efforts. Chariot Artificial Intelligence Private Limited, one of the first four teams selected under the IndiaAI Mission to build sovereign foundation models, developed the models from scratch in India. The Chariot-1 model suite comprises a Large Language Model and a Text-to-Speech model, both pre-trained from scratch in India. The Large Language Model is an 11-billion-parameter Mixture-of-Experts model, while it is available in three variants of 10.7 billion, 1.7 billion and 745 million parameters, catering to different computational requirements and deployment environments. The Text-to-Speech model supports English and 10 Indian languages, including Hindi, Bengali, Marathi, Tamil, Telugu, Kannada, Malayalam, Gujarati, Punjabi and Odia. The model advances context-aware speech generation, recording over 97 per cent verbalisation accuracy on the Async TTS Pronunciation Benchmark. The Chariot team introduced three research innovations to improve training efficiency and multilingual performance. IndicShift, a shared alphabet for Indian scripts, achieves 2.5 times fewer tokens on Indian text. Nested Training allows three model sizes to be developed through a single training run, with 62 per cent faster training. Mixture of Vocabularies delivers 38 per cent faster training. The models incorporate novel research innovations aimed at improving computational efficiency, multilingual capabilities and adaptability across different deployment environments. The initiative reflects the government's commitment to nurturing indigenous AI capabilities, supporting advanced research and enabling the development of AI models that address India's technological, linguistic and societal requirements. Designed to advance language understanding and speech generation, the models incorporate novel research innovations aimed at improving computational efficiency, multilingual capabilities, and adaptability across different deployment environments. Advancing multilingual AI through indigenous research A key highlight of the launch was the presentation of three research innovations developed by the Chariot team and integrated into the training of Chariot-1 models. These innovations address fundamental challenges in language processing and model training, particularly in the context of India's diverse linguistic landscape. IndicShift, an open-source innovation, introduces a shared alphabet for Indian scripts, enabling AI models to leverage similarities across languages rather than treating each script independently. Covering 1,012 characters across 12 Indian scripts through 350 letters, the approach achieves up to 2.5 times fewer tokens on Indian text compared to OpenAI's GPT tokeniser. The research also reports a 5% to 8% improvement in model performance on Indian languages on the same compute, while maintaining performance in English and code. Nested Training enables three complete model sizes to be trained simultaneously through a single training run and one set of weights. This innovation addresses the challenge of developing separate models for different computing environments, enabling deployment across data centres, laptops, smartphones and edge devices. The approach delivers a reported 62 % improvement in training speed compared to training the three model sizes separately. national_raw_news.content: India launches indigenous Chariot-1 Foundation Models to strengthen sovereign AI capabilities Toggle navigation हिंदी खबर India launches indigenous Chariot-1 Foundation Models to strengthen sovereign AI capabilities ANI | Updated: Nov 26, 2026 13:35 IST ANI News Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [India], November 26 (ANI): In a push to strengthen India's sovereign artificial intelligence (AI) capabilities, the Union Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) Secretary S Krishnan launched the indigenously developed Chariot-1 Foundation Models under the IndiaAI Mission, according to a statement by MeitY. According to the release, Chariot Artificial Intelligence Pvt. Ltd. is among the first four teams selected under the IndiaAI Mission to develop sovereign foundation models. The Chariot-1 model suite comprises a Large Language Model (LLM) and a Text-to-Speech (TTS) model, both pre-trained from scratch in India. “Designed to advance language understanding and speech generation, the models incorporate novel research innovations aimed at improving computational efficiency, multilingual capabilities and adaptability across different deployment environments,” the release added. The Chariot-1 LLM is an 11-billion-parameter mixture-of-experts model, with four billion active parameters per token. It is available in three variants of 10.7 billion, 1.7 billion and 745 million parameters, catering to different computational requirements and deployment environments. Meanwhile, the Chariot-1 TTS model is capable of generating speech in English and 10 Indian languages, including Hindi, Bengali, Marathi, Tamil, Telugu, Kannada, Malayalam, Gujarati, Punjabi and Odia, according to the release. One of the key features of the speech model is its ability to understand context and determine how numbers, dates, currencies, units, URLs and abbreviations should be pronounced. According to the ministry, this capability enables more natural and context-aware speech generation, addressing a key challenge in developing speech technologies for real-world applications. The speech model recorded over 97 per cent verbalisation accuracy on the Async TTS Pronunciation Benchmark, which comprises 1,029 real-world sentences and 2,251 instances of non-standard text across 42 categories, the Ministry said. It also recorded a character error rate of 7.60 per cent in Hindi and an average character error rate of 6.47 per cent across nine other Indian languages, the lowest among the systems evaluated in the reported tests. “By supporting teams developing sovereign foundation models, the IndiaAI Mission is enabling researchers, innovators and enterprises to pursue ambitious AI research and translate it into homegrown technological solutions,” the release said. national_raw_news.content: Union Health Ministry observes Constitution Day with collective reading of Preamble, reaffirms allegiance Toggle navigation हिंदी खबर Union Health Ministry observes Constitution Day with collective reading of Preamble, reaffirms allegiance ANI | Updated: Nov 26, 2026 12:53 IST ANI News Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [India], November 26 (ANI): The Union Ministry of Health and Family Welfare observed Constitution Day with a collective reading of the Preamble to the Constitution of India by its officers and officials on Thursday at Kartavya Bhawan in New Delhi. The observance commemorated the adoption of the Constitution of India and reaffirmed the values and ideals enshrined in its Preamble. According of Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, all senior officials, including the ranks of Additional Secretaries, Joint Secretaries, Directors, Deputy Secretaries and equivalent officers of the Department of Health and Family Welfare participated in person in the programme. Other officers and officials of the Ministry, including representatives from the National AIDS Control Organisation (NACO), National Health Authority (NHA) and National Medical Commission (NMC), also joined the programme through video conferencing, as per the release. The observance provided an opportunity for officers and officials of the Ministry to reaffirm their collective commitment to the values enshrined in the Constitution that guide the nation's democratic framework and governance. Constitution Day, also known as Samvidhan Diwas, is observed every year on 26th November to commemorate the adoption of the Constitution of India by the Constituent Assembly on 26th November, 1949. national_raw_news.content: ₹2,014 crore for new Assam Greenfield Airport, ₹4,000 crore boost to Tamil Nadu port: Union Cabinet's big decisions | Mint View Market Dashboard ₹2,014 crore for new Assam Greenfield Airport, ₹4,000 crore boost to Tamil Nadu port: Union Cabinet's big decisions The Union Cabinet approved a ₹ 2,014-crore greenfield airport at Doloo, Assam, and a ₹ 4,288-crore second container terminal at Kamarajar Port, Tamil Nadu. The projects aim to improve regional connectivity, boost trade and tourism, expand port capacity, and support jobs and economic growth. Akriti Anand Updated 26 Nov 2026, 11:53 AM IST Prefer Livemint on Google The Union Cabinet approved ₹2,014 crore for a brand-new Greenfield Airport at Doloo, Assam. ( Jyotiraditya M. Scindia ) AI Quick Read The Union Cabinet gave its nod to a ₹ 2,014-crore greenfield airport at Doloo in Cachar district and over ₹ 4,000 crore for the development of the Second Container Terminal at Kamarajar Port Limited in Tamil Nadu. Here's all you need to know about the two projects: Doloo Greenfield Airport The Union Cabinet approved the development of Greenfield Airport at Doloo, Silchar, Assam at an estimated cost of 2,014 crore. The existing Silchar airport, jointly owned by the Indian Air Force and the Airports Authority of India (AAI), operates a civil enclave spread over 70 acres. “To overcome the severe operational and spatial constraints of the existing defence landlocked civil enclave at Silchar Airport and to accommodate sustained passenger growth, the Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs chaired by the Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi has approved the development of a New Greenfield Airport at Doloo, Silchar, Assam by the Airports Authority of India (AAI) at an estimated cost of Rs.2,014 crore,” a press release by the government stated. It noted the strategic location of Doloo, where the new airport will be built. “Doloo, situated in the Cachar District of Assam, serves as the strategic heart of the Barak Valley — a region renowned for its extensive tea gardens, agro-based industries, and immense potential for eco and cultural tourism,” it added. According to the government, the proposed terminal building will span a total area of 12,351 sqm, with a capacity to handle 800 passengers during peak hours and 1 million passengers per year. View full Image Credit: Bhupender Yadav, PIB It will be designed with modern passenger amenities, sustainable green building principles, and modular expansion capability. In addition, the project encompasses the development of a 2,705m x 45m, Code-4C-compliant runway suitable for A320 aircraft operations, along with the construction of a new Apron capable of parking 6 nos. A-320 aircraft and a dedicated isolation bay. How will this new airport help? The Doloo Greenfield Airport is expected to meet the rapidly growing demands of air traffic in South Assam and adjoining areas of neighbouring States. It is expected to significantly decongest existing infrastructure, unlock regional economic potential by boosting trade and tourism, and offer a world-class gateway integrating Northeast India with broader national and international growth corridors.
